name: The Consequences of Sin

objectives.text: Identify from the story of Adam and Eve hiding in the garden that sin separates people from God
Retell how sin brought pain, hard work, and thorns into God's good world
Name death as the result and wages of sin
Describe how sin broke relationships between people, using Adam blaming Eve and Eve blaming the serpent as an example
Recall that sin makes every person guilty and accountable before God
Summarize the misery of the fallen estate as loss of communion with God, being under His wrath and curse, the miseries of this life, death, and the pains of hell
Explain the difference between the guilt that makes a sinner liable to punishment and the pollution that defiles the sinner's nature
Describe how the whole created order has been placed under a curse and groans because of human sin
Compare physical, spiritual, and eternal death as Scripture describes them
Explain how Scripture describes fallen people as held captive under the power of Satan and the fear of death
Explain from biblical examples that sin brings real consequences in this life even when the sinner is forgiven
Analyze how Romans 1 presents the wrath of God as already revealed in the present through His giving people over to their sinful desires
Distinguish the inward punishments of sin such as blindness of mind and hardness of heart from its outward punishments such as the curse on creation and death itself
Explain why Scripture presents physical death as an enemy and a penalty that entered through sin rather than a natural part of God's original creation
Trace how Christ's redemptive work answers each consequence of sin, including guilt, curse, death, and wrath
Explain the Reformed teaching on hell as everlasting separation from God and conscious punishment, the just penalty for sin
Distinguish God's fatherly discipline of believers who sin from the penal condemnation that falls on the unrepentant
Construct a written synthesis organizing the consequences of sin under guilt, corruption, death, and wrath with supporting Scripture and confessional references
Evaluate universalism and annihilationism against the biblical teaching on final judgment
Defend the Reformed position that eternal punishment is just because sin is committed against the infinite majesty and holiness of God

changes: Kept and reworded the real competencies on separation, death, guilt, the misery of the fallen estate, guilt and pollution, kinds of death, wrath in Romans 1, inward and outward punishments, death as penalty, hell, the fourfold synthesis, universalism and annihilationism, and the justice of eternal punishment. Replaced the vague grade 3 sorrow item with a concrete Genesis 3 retelling at grade 1, and merged the grade 6 cross item and grade 12 synthesis into one objective tracing how Christ answers each consequence. Added missing competencies on broken human relationships, the curse on creation, bondage to Satan, temporal consequences of forgiven sin, and fatherly discipline versus condemnation. Corrected confessional anchors to WLC Q27, Q28, Q29, WCF 6.6, 11.5, 17.3, 33.2, and Heidelberg Q10 to Q12, and kept origin, depravity, and gravity of sin for the sibling sub-topics.
